fomorian.d: one of a group of Celtic sea demons sometimes associated with the hostile power of nature

foment.d: try to stir up public opinion

fomes.d: genus of bracket fungi forming corky or woody perennial shelflike sporophores often of large size; includes some that cause destructive heartrot in trees

fomentation.d: deliberate and intentional triggering (of trouble or discord)

fomite.d: any inanimate object (as a towel or money or clothing or dishes or books or toys etc.) that can transmit infectious agents from one person to another

fomenter.d: one who agitates; a political troublemaker
